dedupe_keys.name: csb investigation philadelphia energy solutions refinery fire and explosions 2019

description: This case study is the U.S. Chemical Safety Board's investigation of the vapour release, fire and multiple explosions in the hydrofluoric acid (HF) alkylation unit of the Philadelphia Energy Solutions refinery in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, at about 4 a.m. on 21 June 2019. It was carried out by the U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board (CSB), which released its final report on 11 October 2022. The CSB page offers the final report, appendices, factual updates, animations and the safety video Wake Up Call, all free. Caveats: the page read does not give injury counts or confirm the quantity of HF released, and CSB findings are not enforcement decisions. The CSB issued five recommendations: protect critical safety systems from fire and explosion, install remotely operated emergency isolation valves on HF and hydrocarbon vessels, strengthen EPA inspections of HF alkylation units, and analyse safer alkylation technologies; two were still open at access. For simulation it is a reference event for toxic release hazard exposure, emergency response and the cascading loss of regional fuel supply when a large refinery closes. It is related to the CSB West Fertilizer explosion record in this catalogue, another CSB post-event analysis.
